decision.conviction_rationale: The business quality is genuine — 70% gross margins, durable pricing power, and a blue-chip institutional cluster buying at a 37% discount to the 52-week high — but I cannot place an honest entry today. The market sold the beat on volume, Q4 estimates are being cut, and the chart is a confirmed downtrend. The Street's average target is $87, only 3.8% above the current price, and the high is $115 from just one analyst — not enough of a consensus runway to justify entry with no chart support. LOW conviction here means I'm tracking it, not trading it.
decision.core_belief: Zoetis owns the strongest franchise in animal health — 70% gross margins, pricing power across pets and livestock, and a pipeline that just added a next-generation 75-day itch-relief antibody in Cytopoint Plus. The business is under real pressure right now from generic competition in dermatology, softer vet visit volumes, and a companion animal market that is repricing in a cost-conscious consumer environment, but those are cyclical and competitive headwinds, not franchise destruction. What has to stay true: gross margins hold at or above 70%, the livestock and diagnostics segments keep growing to offset companion animal softness, and new products like Cytopoint Plus extend pricing power in dermatology over time.

decision.rationale: Zoetis reported a clean adjusted EPS beat on November 5 — 14–16% above estimates with a revenue beat and a full-year EPS guidance raise — but the stock gapped down 4.8% on 2.5× volume on report day and fell another 3.8% the next session. That gap-down-on-a-beat is a hard disqualifier for the post-earnings drift setup: the market is saying the numbers weren't enough, and earnings revisions for Q4 are running 0 up / 5 down. The chart is a confirmed downtrend with the 200-day falling at $91.48, the Trend Template scores 2/8, and no moving-average pullback setup applies. I'm watching the stock, not buying it today. What would change that: the companion animal franchise stabilizing (Q1 2027 report, around February 10), the 200-day turning flat, and Q4 estimate revisions reversing upward. The 13F institutional cluster — Davis at $249M, Gayner 5×, Tweedy and First Eagle opening — and the new Cytopoint Plus USDA license keep the business interesting enough to track; those quality value managers typically buy durable franchises at multi-year discounts, not broken ones.

triggers.rationale: The February 2027 Q4 report is the first real test of whether companion animal is stabilizing and whether Cytopoint Plus is gaining traction — I want to look at the setup and estimates a week before it prints.
A close above the base pivot at $89.29 would mean the stock has reclaimed its November high on the way out of the downtrend — that's the first technical signal worth pricing a buy against.

decision.variant_view: The sell-side consensus is 27% Buy, and most of the neutral crowd is waiting for companion animal to stabilize before turning constructive. But their time horizon is 3–5 years, not 60 days, and I need a chart setup that isn't in a downtrend before I can trade alongside them on a swing basis.

decision.rationale: HeartFlow reported Q3 2026 yesterday — EPS of -$0.03 vs. the -$0.10 estimate, a 71% beat, with revenue up 57% year-over-year to $72.9M. The stock opened sharply higher but closed today down 17.7% to $49.31, giving back most of the gap. That gap-day collapse means the PEAD setup is gone — the market is not under-reacting to good news, it is actively selling it. Three analysts raised price targets today (Canaccord to $69, Stifel to $70, Baird to $68), which lifts the street's average well above the stale $48.50 consensus, and implies real upside from here — but the stock needs to find a floor first. The prior pass in August was on a weaker chart and slower business momentum; what's changed is 57% revenue growth, expanding gross margins (83.6%), and a raised full-year guide. The setup that fits now is a pullback-to-rising-average entry once the stock stabilizes. The 50-day at $51.94 is rising and roughly 5% above today's close of $49.31; a hold near that level on calming volume is the entry I want to price. I'm watching for the stock to find its footing near the 50-day before writing a buy.
decision.conviction_rationale: The business is genuinely accelerating — 57% revenue growth, 83.6% gross margins, and a beat that drove three analyst target raises to $68–70 today. That puts the refreshed street high at $70 against today's $49.31, meaningful upside if the stock stabilizes. But the gap-day reversal (opened near $60, closed at $49) is a warning: the market wanted more, or sellers were waiting. I want to see the 50-day hold before committing capital. This is medium conviction until the chart confirms buyers are back.
decision.core_belief: HeartFlow makes AI-powered cardiac imaging software — specifically FFR-CT, which lets cardiologists assess coronary artery disease from a CT scan without an invasive catheterization. The company earns revenue from per-analysis fees and enterprise contracts with hospitals and health systems, growing fast as clinical guidelines and payer coverage expand. The case rests on continued adoption growth translating into revenue at 80%+ gross margins, with the path to profitability shortening each quarter.
decision.variant_view: Analysts who set targets before yesterday's report were anchored to $45–55; the three who updated today jumped to $68–70, suggesting the street is still catching up to 57% revenue growth and 83.6% gross margins. The consensus average ($48.50, stale) sits below today's price — the market doesn't yet price in the upgraded targets, and if revisions follow broadly, the stock has a wide lane to reprice upward.
